newsitem.title: UK: UK parties to meet tv chiefs over election debate.
newsitem.headline: UK parties to meet tv chiefs over election debate.

text.p: Britain's Conservative, Labour and Liberal Democrat parties were meeting broadcasting chiefs on Monday to try to settle a format for the country's first live television election debate between political leaders.
The debates have been timetabled for April 13, 20 and 27 and agreement would have to be concluded by the end of this week if the necessary arrangements are to be put in place.

So far, the proposals put forward suggest a 90-minute head-to-head debate between Labour's Tony Blair and Prime Minister John Major with Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown interviewed in between. There would be an audience but no direct questions to the three leaders.

But negotiations have been bogged down by Ashdown's insistence on a full role in the debate. The Scottish National Party is also insisting that any debates screened in Scotland should "reflect the reality of four-party politics north of the border."
